title: How Far Is Too Far? Object Recognition Declines Monotonically with Semantic Distance
claim: A benchmark that recomposes objects and backgrounds along a graded semantic-distance axis reveals a smooth, monotonic drop in recognition accuracy.
layout: 3 panels: dataset variants top-left, insertion grid bottom-left, accuracy plots right; green-to-red gradient bar
description: A wide figure with three panels split by dashed gray lines. Panel (a), top left, shows a jacamar photo, an arrow to its inpainted background, then a plus sign and four object-only variants (transparent cutout, black, white and 1/f-noise backgrounds). Dataset statistics sit at the right: 1,137 backgrounds, 25 subcategories, 918 object classes, about 14M composites. Panel (b), below, is a 2x5 grid of composite photos. The rows are a jacamar branch and a living room with a television. The columns are ranks 50, 250, 500, 750 and 950, with borders and labels shifting from green to red. Inserted objects range from a bee and a piano to a shell and a salamander. A gradient bar underneath runs from Congruent to Incongruent. Panel (c), on the right, has two stacked line plots of Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy against semantic dissimilarity rank. Six colored model curves decline steadily, and Orig. markers sit at the top left.
caption: ImageNet-OOC1k enables controlled recomposition along a visual-semantic axis. (a) Dataset overview. ImageNet-S masks [ref] are used to construct original images, inpainted backgrounds, and object-only variants, including crops and composites on black, white, and $1/f$ noise backgrounds. (b) Objects are inserted at increasing semantic distance ranks relative to the original class. The example backgrounds (jacamar, television) use the same ranks (50, 250, 500, 750, 950), but different inserted objects because distance is defined relationally. (c) Top-1 accuracy decreases monotonically with semantic distance rank (bin width 25) for representative models (ViT-B/16, ViT-L/16, DeiT-B/16, ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B3, CLIP ViT-B/16). Colored markers (Orig.) show original-image accuracy. Top-5 accuracy follows the same trend, indicating that semantic mismatch affects the broader class ranking.
abstract: Vision models are sensitive to object-background context, yet it remains unclear how recognition changes as the semantic distance between objects and backgrounds increases. We introduce ImageNet-OOC1k, a benchmark enabling graded control of object-background relationships along a continuous consensus visual-semantic dissimilarity axis. This formulation reveals a highly consistent monotonic decline in recognition accuracy across 35 models spanning convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, and vision-language models. Internal analyses of Vision Transformers reveal patterns consistent with aggregation failure, where object evidence is present at the patch level but not consolidated into the final prediction. Using this characterization as a diagnostic probe, a simple spatial re-ranking strategy recovers a subset of these errors and improves in-sample accuracy by up to 5.7 percentage points. These results establish context sensitivity as a continuous and predictable property of modern vision systems, with Vision Transformer analyses suggesting that aggregation limitations may contribute to some failure types even when object evidence remains available.
